what_its_for: Nystatin is an antifungal medicine used to treat fungal infections caused by a yeast called Candida. It can treat infections in your mouth (thrush), throat, intestines, and skin. It works by killing or stopping the growth of the fungus causing your infection.
how_to_take: How you take nystatin depends on what form your doctor prescribed: LIQUID (Suspension): Shake the bottle well before each use. Use the measuring dropper or spoon that comes with your medicine. Place half the dose in each side of your mouth. Swish it around your mouth as long as you can, then swallow it. Do not eat or drink anything for at least 5 minutes after taking it. LOZENGES (Pastilles): Let the lozenge dissolve slowly in your mouth. Do not chew or swallow it whole. TABLETS: Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. POWDER or CREAM (for skin): Clean and dry the affected skin area first. Apply a thin layer to the affected area and surrounding skin. Do not cover with tight bandages unless your doctor tells you to. Take nystatin at evenly spaced times throughout the day to keep a steady amount in your body.
dosing: Your dose will depend on the type and severity of your infection and the form of nystatin you are using. Your doctor will tell you exactly how much to take and how many times a day. Common dosing examples include: Mouth or throat infections in adults: 400,000 to 600,000 units (liquid) swished and swallowed 4 times a day. Skin infections: Apply cream or powder 2 to 3 times daily. Always follow your doctor or pharmacist's specific instructions. Do not take more or less than prescribed. Complete the full course of treatment even if you feel better, so the infection does not come back.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store nystatin liquid in the refrigerator or at room temperature — check your specific product label, as instructions may vary. Keep it away from heat and direct sunlight. Do not freeze the liquid unless the label says it is okay to do so. Store tablets, powder, and cream at room temperature in a cool, dry place away from moisture and heat. Keep the container tightly closed. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Do not use nystatin after the expiration date printed on the label. Ask your pharmacist how to safely dispose of unused medicine.
what_to_avoid: Do not eat or drink anything for at least 5 minutes after using the liquid form so the medicine has time to work in your mouth. Avoid wearing tight-fitting or synthetic underwear or clothing over skin infections, as moisture can make fungal infections worse. Try to keep affected skin areas clean and dry. If you are treating a vaginal infection, avoid sexual intercourse during treatment unless your doctor says it is okay. Avoid sharing your medicine with anyone else, even if they have similar symptoms. Do not stop taking nystatin early just because you feel better — finishing the full course is important.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor if you notice any of the following: Your symptoms do not improve within a few days of starting treatment. Your symptoms get worse or your infection spreads. You develop a rash, hives, itching, or swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat, which could be a sign of a rare allergic reaction — seek emergency help right away if this happens. You have difficulty breathing or swallowing. You experience nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, or diarrhea that is severe or does not go away. You have any new or unusual symptoms that concern you.
when_it_works: Most people begin to feel better within a few days of starting nystatin. Mouth and throat infections usually start improving within 2 to 3 days. Skin infections may take up to 1 to 2 weeks to fully clear up. Even if you feel better quickly, it is very important to finish the entire course of treatment your doctor prescribed. Stopping too early may allow the fungus to come back and become harder to treat.
special_populations: Pregnant or breastfeeding women: Nystatin is generally considered safe to use during pregnancy and breastfeeding, especially for skin or mouth infections. However, always tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding before using any medication. Children and infants: Nystatin is commonly used in infants and children for oral thrush. For babies, the liquid is usually placed gently in the cheeks using a dropper. Follow your pediatrician's instructions carefully about the correct dose for your child's age and weight. Older adults: No special dose changes are usually needed, but always let your doctor know all the medicines you are taking to avoid any interactions. People with weakened immune systems: If you have HIV, cancer, diabetes, or are taking medicines that weaken your immune system, tell your doctor, as you may need a longer course of treatment or additional monitoring.
